title: Dar Al Kahrbaa
description: A specialized learning platform for electrical-engineering training across web and Android.
cardDescription: A custom electrical-engineering LMS connecting course discovery, student enrollment, video learning, payments, and administration across web and Android.
overview: Dar Al Kahrbaa turns a specialized electrical-engineering training concept into a custom LMS connecting course discovery, student enrollment, video learning, payments, and platform administration.

headings.challenge: Specialized engineering education needed a learning platform built around its own courses and students.
headings.build: A custom LMS connecting students, courses, content, payments, and administration.
headings.outcome: Dar Al Kahrbaa turned an early education concept into a complete specialized learning platform.

problem:
The client wanted to create a dedicated digital learning experience for electrical-engineering students, trainees, and professionals rather than rely on a generic content platform.

The system needed to support student registration, structured course enrollment, video lessons, educational materials, electronic payments, and centralized administration.

It also needed an architecture capable of supporting a growing student base as the education offering expanded.

The challenge was to turn an early product concept into a complete learning-management system across web and mobile.
solution:
Oraixen designed and developed Dar Al Kahrbaa from the platform strategy and LMS architecture through the web experience, Android application, backend services, APIs, payment integration, video delivery, and administration.

Students can register, explore specialized electrical-engineering courses, enroll, and access video lessons and educational materials through the platform.

The course catalog includes specialized training designed for electrical-engineering students and field professionals, including accredited courses.

Administrators manage users, courses, content, and learning-platform activity from a central dashboard.
impact:
Students can discover courses, enroll, pay, and access learning content through connected web and Android experiences instead of relying on disconnected tools.

At the operational level, the administration team can manage users, courses, content, and platform activity from one central environment.

The custom LMS architecture was designed to support continued growth in the student base and expansion of the electrical-engineering training offering.

title: Duvdu
description: A connected marketplace for booking and managing media-production projects from agreement to final delivery.
cardDescription: A marketplace connecting clients and creative service providers through booking, project milestones, asset delivery, and escrow-backed payments.
overview: Duvdu brings clients and creative service providers into one workflow for discovering talent, agreeing on project terms, booking schedules, managing milestones, delivering assets, and releasing payments through escrow.

headings.challenge: Creative projects involve more than finding the right talent.
headings.build: One workflow connecting clients, creators, projects, and payments.
headings.outcome: Duvdu turned a fragmented creative-production process into a connected digital workflow.

problem: Clients and creative professionals were coordinating requirements, schedules, deliverables, contracts, and payments across disconnected channels. That created several points of risk: unclear expectations, missed delivery dates, payment concerns, and limited visibility into the status of a project once work had started. The client wanted Duvdu to provide a structured marketplace where both sides could manage the full project lifecycle in one place.
solution: Oraixen designed and built the platform across web and mobile, supported by a central backend and administration system. Clients can discover service providers, review portfolios, agree on the work, schedule projects, and manage delivery through the platform. Service providers can build their profiles and portfolios, publish previous work, identify collaborators and equipment used, manage bookings, and deliver project assets directly through Duvdu. The platform connects those interactions to project contracts, milestones, deadlines, and an escrow-based payment workflow.
impact: Instead of managing discovery, agreements, scheduling, file delivery, and payments through separate channels, clients and service providers can move through the project lifecycle inside one platform. The escrow workflow also connects payment release to project delivery and client approval, reducing payment risk for both sides.

title: Discount Emy
description: A mobile marketplace connecting students and parents with active educational discounts from partner schools and universities.
cardDescription: A mobile marketplace connecting students and parents with educational discounts from partner schools and universities, backed by centralized request and commission management.
overview: Discount Emy transformed an offline partner network and Facebook-group workflow into a structured mobile platform for educational offers, applicant requests, partner listings, and commission tracking.

headings.challenge: Educational discounts were being managed through social posts instead of a dedicated operating platform.
headings.build: A mobile marketplace connecting educational offers, applicants, partners, and administration.
headings.outcome: Discount Emy moved an educational-discount operation from Facebook posts into a dedicated mobile marketplace.

problem:
The business had built an offline network of schools and universities offering contracted discounts, but customers primarily discovered those offers through a Facebook group and manual communication.

That made it harder to keep active discounts organized, communicate changes quickly, manage growing demand, and maintain a structured view of applicant requests and partner-related commission activity.

The challenge was to move the business from a social-group workflow into a dedicated digital marketplace that could serve parents and students while giving the internal team central control over educational offers and incoming requests.
solution:
Oraixen designed and developed Discount Emy across iOS and Android, supported by backend services, APIs, and a central administration platform.

Parents, students, and applicants can browse participating educational institutions and view current discount programs related to school and university admissions and fees.

Behind the customer experience, the administration system allows the business to manage educational partner listings, publish and update discount offers, follow incoming requests, and track commission-related activity linked to its partner model.

The result is a structured digital workflow that replaces dependence on manually maintained social posts.
impact:
Parents and students can access current educational offers through a purpose-built mobile experience rather than depending on manually maintained social posts.

At the operational level, the business can manage educational partners, discount programs, applicant requests, and commission-related activity through a central administration system.

The platform also created a structured foundation for handling growing demand without relying on the original Facebook-group workflow.

title: Order FS
description: A custom single-vendor commerce platform connecting shopping, orders, customer data, and store operations across web and mobile.
cardDescription: A custom single-vendor commerce platform connecting shopping, orders, customers, and centralized store operations across web, iOS, and Android.
overview: Order FS was built around the requirements of a retail business in Kuwait, connecting the customer journey across responsive web, iOS, and Android with a centralized backend and administration platform.

headings.challenge: The retailer needed a commerce platform built around its own operating model rather than a generic storefront.
headings.build: One custom commerce platform connecting customers and retail operations.
headings.outcome: Order FS turned a retail concept into one connected commerce and operations platform for the Kuwaiti market.

problem:
The client had a clear business concept for launching a custom single-vendor e-commerce operation in Kuwait.

The platform needed to support a connected customer experience across responsive web, iOS, and Android while giving the internal team central control over products, customers, orders, fulfillment-related workflows, and commerce analytics.

The challenge was to turn those business requirements into one tailored commerce system where the customer-facing channels and internal operations worked from the same platform foundation.
solution:
Oraixen mapped the business requirements, designed the product experience, and developed Order FS across responsive web, iOS, Android, backend services, APIs, integrations, and administration.

Customers can browse the retailer’s product catalog, add items to their cart, move through checkout, and place orders through the digital shopping experience.

Store teams use the centralized administration platform to manage catalog information, customer records, orders, fulfillment-related activity, and available commerce analytics.

The platform was designed specifically around a single retailer’s operating model and Kuwaiti market requirements rather than a multi-vendor marketplace structure.
impact:
Customers can move from product discovery through cart, checkout, and ordering across web and mobile experiences connected to the same platform foundation.

At the operational level, store teams can manage products, customers, orders, and fulfillment-related activity from a central administration environment.

The result is a tailored single-vendor system built around the retailer’s own operating requirements instead of a generic or multi-vendor commerce model.

title: Maat VIP
description: A digital sourcing portal connecting international business requirements with China-based procurement, custom manufacturing, quality control, and logistics.
cardDescription: A China sourcing portal connecting international procurement and custom-manufacturing requests with factory sourcing, QA, and logistics.
overview: Oraixen built Maat’s digital entry point for global sourcing inquiries and established a strategic partnership connecting technology delivery with Maat’s factory, manufacturing, QA, and logistics capabilities in China.

headings.challenge: A strong China sourcing operation needed a digital entry point for international business demand.
headings.build: A sourcing portal and partnership model connecting digital demand with physical supply-chain execution.
headings.outcome: Maat gained a digital gateway for global sourcing demand, while the partnership connected Oraixen’s technology work with supply-chain capability in China.

problem:
Maat already operated a sourcing and logistics network in China covering factory procurement, manufacturing coordination, quality-control workflows, and shipping.

What it lacked was a dedicated digital platform that clearly presented those capabilities and gave importers and enterprises a structured way to submit sourcing and custom-manufacturing requirements.

The opportunity also extended beyond the website itself. Oraixen and Maat wanted to establish a working model that connected Oraixen’s technology capability with direct access to China-based sourcing and manufacturing operations.
solution:
Oraixen designed and developed Maat’s public web experience, sourcing inquiry journey, backend services, APIs, and administration tools.

Businesses can submit procurement, sourcing, sample-based manufacturing, and custom-production requirements through the platform.

Those inquiries can then enter Maat’s sourcing operation in China, where relevant workflows may include factory sourcing, manufacturing coordination, sample verification, quality-control processes, and logistics.

Alongside the platform, Oraixen and Maat established a strategic technology and sourcing partnership that connects suitable digital and enterprise projects with Maat’s China supply-chain capability.
impact:
International businesses can submit sourcing and manufacturing requirements through a structured digital journey instead of relying only on informal inquiry channels.

Maat’s team receives those requirements through a platform connected to its China-based sourcing, manufacturing, quality-control, and logistics operation.

For Oraixen, the partnership also creates a direct route to physical sourcing and manufacturing capability for suitable enterprise projects that require both technology and supply-chain execution.

cardDescription: A home-services marketplace connecting homeowners with verified craftsmen, contractors, payments, job tracking, and engineering supervision.

headings.outcome: Maqdya turned an informal home-services hiring process into a structured digital marketplace.

Homeowners could find it difficult to evaluate craftsmen and contractors before starting maintenance, finishing, or renovation work.

Service quality, pricing expectations, communication, and project follow-up could vary significantly when the entire process happened through informal offline channels.

For larger renovation and construction work, the client also wanted professional engineering supervision to provide more structured follow-up across project phases.

The goal was to turn an informal hiring process into a marketplace where customers could discover providers, review previous work, communicate, pay, and follow the job through a structured digital workflow.
solution:
Oraixen built Maqdya from the ground up across web, iOS, Android, backend services, APIs, and administration.

Customers can explore service categories, review provider profiles and portfolios, read customer reviews, communicate directly with service providers, and manage service requests through the platform.

Service providers can present their experience and previous work and participate in a structured job workflow rather than relying entirely on informal offline communication.

The system also connects supported electronic payments, order and job tracking, and engineering-supervision workflows for projects that require professional oversight.
impact:
Customers can discover providers, review previous work, communicate, create service requests, complete supported payments, and follow jobs through one connected platform.

Service providers gain a structured digital presence for presenting their work and managing customer opportunities.

For projects that need additional oversight, engineering supervision adds a professional follow-up layer across the work lifecycle.

title: Waffar Cash
industry: On-Demand Delivery / Hyperlocal Super App / Multi-Vendor Marketplace
description: A hyperlocal Super App connecting customers, merchants, and delivery riders through multi-vendor ordering and single-trip delivery.
cardDescription: A hyperlocal multi-vendor platform connecting customers, merchants, and riders, with eligible nearby-store orders combined into a single delivery trip.
overview: Waffar Cash was designed for local commerce in Al-Qantarah, Sinai, bringing restaurants, supermarkets, pharmacies, cafes, customers, and delivery riders into one operating platform. Its multi-store model allows eligible nearby orders to be combined into a single delivery trip.
statusNote: Project halted due to local regulatory and security conditions.

headings.challenge: Local delivery was fragmented across merchants, riders, and separate customer orders.
headings.build: A multi-vendor Super App built around local ordering and delivery operations.
headings.outcome: Waffar Cash brought fragmented hyperlocal ordering and delivery into one multi-sided operating platform.

problem:
Restaurants and other local merchants in Al-Qantarah could struggle to coordinate delivery riders, contributing to delayed, incorrect, or cold deliveries.

Customers ordering from more than one nearby store also faced separate delivery flows and duplicated delivery costs when each merchant had to be handled independently.

At the same time, restaurants, supermarkets, pharmacies, and cafes had no single local digital platform connecting commerce and delivery operations.

The challenge was to create one hyperlocal ecosystem where customers, merchants, riders, and administrators could operate through the same platform.
solution:
Oraixen designed and developed Waffar Cash as a connected platform spanning separate customer, merchant, and rider applications, together with backend services, APIs, merchant operations, and administration.

Customers can order across multiple local categories, including restaurants, supermarkets, pharmacies, and cafes, as well as submit supported custom errand requests.

The platform's distinctive multi-store workflow allows eligible orders from nearby participating stores to be combined into one delivery trip instead of generating separate delivery trips for each merchant.

Merchants manage incoming order activity through their dedicated tools, while delivery riders participate through a separate delivery application and administrators oversee the wider platform operation.
impact:
Customers could order across several local commerce categories while merchants and delivery riders worked through dedicated operational experiences connected to the same backend.

For eligible nearby multi-store orders, the batching workflow reduced the need for separate delivery trips and duplicated delivery charges by combining the order into one delivery journey.

The product also established an architecture capable of supporting a broader local Super App model, although the project was later halted due to local regulatory and security conditions.

title: Gefires
industry: B2B E-Commerce / Fire Safety & Firefighting Equipment Sourcing
description: A B2B procurement platform connecting Saudi commercial buyers with fire-safety equipment sourcing, RFQs, quotations, and cross-border logistics from China.
cardDescription: A B2B procurement platform connecting Saudi commercial buyers with fire-safety equipment, custom RFQs, China sourcing, and freight-aware quotations.
overview: Gefires digitizes the commercial procurement journey for fire-alarm, firefighting, and safety equipment, connecting product discovery and bulk quotation requests with China-based sourcing and freight-aware fulfillment workflows.

headings.challenge: Cross-border fire-safety procurement needed a structured digital workflow from product discovery to quotation and fulfillment.
headings.build: A B2B catalog and RFQ platform connecting commercial demand with sourcing and logistics.
headings.outcome: Gefires turned a traditional cross-border procurement process into one connected B2B quotation and sourcing workflow.

problem:
The business was already supplying fire-alarm and firefighting equipment from Chinese factories to commercial buyers in Saudi Arabia, but the procurement process did not have a dedicated B2B digital portal.

Hotels, restaurants, contractors, commercial developers, and enterprise facilities needed a clearer way to browse available equipment and submit bulk purchasing requirements.

The operation also needed quotation workflows that could bring product requirements, sourcing costs, and applicable China-to-Saudi freight considerations into one process.

The challenge was to turn a traditional procurement operation into a connected B2B portal without reducing a complex commercial purchase to a consumer-style checkout flow.
solution:
Oraixen designed and developed Gefires as a web-based procurement platform with a B2B product catalog, custom RFQ engine, backend services, APIs, and central administration.

Commercial buyers can browse relevant fire-safety and firefighting equipment, define bulk requirements, and submit quotation requests through a structured digital journey.

The quotation workflow can account for applicable sourcing and freight components associated with supplying equipment from China to Saudi Arabia.

On the operational side, Gefires teams can manage catalogs, review incoming RFQs, prepare custom proposals, and follow sourcing and shipment-related activity through the administration platform.
impact:
Commercial buyers can now move from equipment discovery to bulk RFQ submission through a dedicated digital portal instead of relying entirely on offline procurement communication.

Gefires teams can manage product information, quotation requests, proposals, and sourcing-related operational follow-up from a central administration environment.

The platform connects Saudi commercial demand with China-based sourcing and freight considerations while keeping the complex commercial purchase centered around quotation rather than generic consumer checkout.

overview: Rosto gives the restaurant its own digital ordering channel, connecting menu discovery, direct orders, real-time order-status updates, delivery operations, and central management in one platform.

headings.challenge: The restaurant needed its own ordering channel and more control over the delivery journey.
headings.build: A connected customer-ordering and delivery ecosystem built around the restaurant's own operation.
headings.outcome: Rosto moved direct ordering and delivery operations into one restaurant-owned digital platform.

problem:
Rosto was already operating as an established restaurant chain, but it did not have a proprietary digital ordering and delivery ecosystem.

Customer orders depended on traditional channels and third-party delivery options, limiting the restaurant's control over the digital customer experience and its delivery operations.

The business needed a dedicated channel where customers could browse the menu, order directly, follow order progress, and receive delivery, while management could oversee menus, active orders, and drivers from one operational environment.
solution:
Oraixen mapped the restaurant's ordering and delivery cycle and built Rosto's digital platform across the customer application, dedicated delivery-driver application, backend services, APIs, and central administration.

Customers can browse the digital menu, select items, complete their order, and follow real-time order-status updates from preparation through delivery.

Delivery riders receive assigned orders through their own mobile experience, use the information needed to complete the delivery journey, and confirm delivery.

Restaurant management uses the operations dashboard to manage menus, monitor active orders, oversee delivery activity, and review sales analytics.
impact:
Customers can browse the menu, place orders directly, and follow order progress through Rosto's own mobile experience instead of depending entirely on traditional or third-party ordering channels.

Delivery drivers operate through a dedicated application connected to the same backend, while restaurant management can oversee menu, order, and delivery activity from a central dashboard.

Following launch, the client reports continued growth in active app usage and daily order volume.

title: IBDL
description: An enterprise training and certification platform replacing a developer-dependent legacy system with self-service ERP, CRM, and administration workflows.
cardDescription: An enterprise training platform replacing developer-dependent legacy administration with self-service ERP, CRM, certification, staff, and training-center workflows.
overview: IBDL brings training-center operations, trainee records, attendance, certificates, staff administration, CRM activity, course content, and commerce workflows into one enterprise platform.

headings.challenge: Routine business operations depended on developers instead of the administration team.
headings.build: A self-service enterprise platform built around the organization’s real operating workflows.
headings.outcome: IBDL replaced a developer-dependent legacy workflow with a self-service enterprise operating platform.

problem:
The existing platform had become difficult to operate and maintain, with bugs, known security weaknesses, and an administrative interface that did not support routine staff workflows effectively.

Basic operational tasks could require a backend developer to run manual database queries, creating unnecessary dependency on engineering resources for everyday administration.

At the same time, training centers, trainee records, course content, attendance, certificates, employees, CRM activity, and commerce operations needed to be managed through a more connected enterprise system.

The challenge was not simply to redesign the website. It was to replace the legacy operational platform and re-engineer how the organization managed its day-to-day work.
solution:
Oraixen audited the existing system, re-engineered the core business flows, and built a replacement platform spanning the public website, enterprise administration, backend services, APIs, ERP capabilities, CRM workflows, and a new database architecture.

Training-center teams can manage centers, branches, groups, trainees, course materials, attendance, and certificates through the administrative platform.

Internal teams can also manage employees, roles, permissions, and attendance, while CRM and commerce capabilities support public course offerings and related customer and sales activity.

Most importantly, routine administrative operations that previously required direct database intervention can now be performed by authorized staff through the system itself.
impact:
Administrative teams can now manage routine training, trainee, certification, staff, CRM, and commerce operations directly through the platform instead of depending on developers for everyday database intervention.

The rebuild also removed the organization’s reliance on the previous legacy architecture and its known operational and security weaknesses.

The result is a more maintainable operating model where technical teams can focus on engineering while authorized business users manage routine operations through the product itself.

title: GoVet
description: A pet-care platform combining e-commerce, home veterinary visit booking, and clinic discovery across iOS and Android.
cardDescription: A pet-care platform combining product ordering, home veterinary visit booking, and clinic discovery across iOS and Android.
overview: GoVet brings pet supplies, home veterinary appointments, branch and clinic discovery, orders, and platform operations into one connected mobile ecosystem.

headings.challenge: Pet owners needed one digital experience for both everyday supplies and veterinary services.
headings.build: One mobile ecosystem connecting pet commerce and veterinary-service booking.
headings.outcome: GoVet brought pet-product ordering and veterinary-service booking into one connected mobile platform.

problem:
The client had a concept for bringing pet-product shopping and veterinary service booking into one mobile platform.

Pet owners needed a simpler way to buy food, accessories, and everyday pet-care items while also arranging home veterinary visits for examinations and routine vaccinations.

The product also needed to help customers discover GoVet branches and partner clinic locations without treating commerce and veterinary services as completely separate journeys.

Behind the customer experience, the business needed centralized administration for products, orders, fulfillment, and veterinary appointments.
solution:
Oraixen designed and developed GoVet from the solution architecture and UI/UX through the iOS and Android applications, backend services, APIs, and administration platform.

Customers can browse and order pet-care products, arrange supported veterinary visits at home, and find GoVet branches or partner clinic locations through the same mobile experience.

Veterinary visit workflows support scheduling for services such as examinations, health checkups, and routine vaccinations.

The administration platform gives the operations team central control over catalog data, customer orders, fulfillment activity, veterinary bookings, and location information.
impact:
Pet owners can use one customer experience to shop for everyday pet-care products, arrange supported home veterinary visits, and discover physical branches and partner clinics.

At the operational level, the business can manage products, orders, fulfillment activity, veterinary bookings, and location information through a centralized administration environment.

The result is a unified pet-care journey that reduces the fragmentation between buying supplies and arranging veterinary services.

title: Nice One
description: A unified beauty-commerce platform connecting online shopping, multi-channel sales, customer data, and order operations in one system.
cardDescription: A beauty-commerce platform bringing online and supported off-platform orders, customer data, and order tracking into one operational system.
overview: Nice One brings the customer shopping experience and internal sales operations into one connected platform across web, mobile, backend, and administration. Orders from supported off-platform channels can also be captured inside the same operational workflow.

headings.challenge: Sales were happening across channels, but the operation had no single source of truth.
headings.build: One commerce platform for customers, orders, and operational data.
headings.outcome: Nice One brought fragmented sales activity into a more centralized commerce and operations workflow.

problem:
Customer conversations and sales activity were spread across channels such as WhatsApp and other off-platform interactions.

That made it difficult for store teams to keep customer records in one place, create orders consistently, and track sales through a unified workflow.

The business needed more than an online storefront. It needed a connected commerce system that served customers through web and mobile while giving the internal team centralized control over orders and customer data.
solution:
Oraixen contributed to the design and development of the Nice One commerce platform across web, iOS, Android, backend services, APIs, and administration.

Customers can browse the product catalog, add products to their cart, complete checkout, and place orders through the digital storefront.

For store teams, the administration system provides a central place to manage customer records and sales orders.

Orders originating through supported off-platform channels, including WhatsApp-based sales, can also be created manually inside the system so they become part of the same order-management workflow.
impact:
Instead of keeping online orders, supported off-platform sales, and customer information across disconnected channels, the platform gives the business one system for capturing orders, maintaining customer records, and tracking sales activity.

This creates a clearer operational view for store teams while giving customers a structured shopping experience across web and mobile.

title: Sanar
description: A connected healthcare platform for telemedicine and on-demand medical services delivered at home.
cardDescription: A healthcare ecosystem connecting telemedicine, at-home medical services, real-time booking, payments, and insurance workflows.
overview: Sanar connects patients, healthcare providers, administrators, payments, and insurance workflows through one digital ecosystem spanning web and mobile. Patients can book remote consultations and at-home healthcare services based on provider availability and appointment schedules.

headings.challenge: Accessing healthcare at home required a more connected service and booking model.
headings.build: One healthcare ecosystem connecting remote consultations and care delivered at home.
headings.outcome: Sanar turned separate healthcare journeys into one connected digital ecosystem.

problem:
Patients needed a convenient way to access services such as home laboratory tests, nursing visits, physical therapy, child vaccinations, and remote medical consultations without relying on a hospital or clinic visit for every interaction.

The platform also needed to coordinate healthcare-provider availability, appointment scheduling, payments, and insurance coverage through a single digital journey.

The challenge was not simply to build an appointment app. It was to connect patients, healthcare providers, home-care services, telemedicine, administration, payments, and insurance workflows into one operating ecosystem.
solution:
Oraixen contributed to the design and development of Sanar across web, iOS, Android, backend services, APIs, and administration.

Patients can browse available healthcare services, choose appointments based on provider availability, book home-care visits, schedule remote consultations, and complete payments through the platform.

The system also connects healthcare workflows with integrated insurance providers, enabling eligible services to operate within insurance-supported coverage and claim-processing flows.

Administrators manage the platform centrally while healthcare providers participate in scheduled appointments and service delivery.
impact:
Patients can access telemedicine and at-home healthcare services through one platform instead of coordinating appointments, service availability, payments, and insurance through separate channels.

Healthcare providers, administrators, insurance integrations, and patient-facing services operate through the same connected platform architecture.

The ecosystem also supports multiple insurance and corporate partner relationships as part of its operating model.

title: Ghiras Al Usrah
description: A digital counseling platform connecting appointment booking, consultant schedules, payments, and hybrid in-person and video consultations.
cardDescription: A counseling platform replacing paper and Excel workflows with digital booking, consultant scheduling, payments, reminders, and hybrid consultations.
overview: Ghiras Al Usrah replaced a paper and spreadsheet-based consultation workflow with a connected platform across web and mobile. Clients can book consultations and make payments digitally, while consultants manage availability and appointments through a dedicated app.

headings.challenge: Consultations were being managed through paper and spreadsheets instead of one operational system.
headings.build: One platform for booking, scheduling, payments, and hybrid consultations.
headings.outcome: Ghiras Al Usrah replaced a fragmented manual consultation process with one digital operating platform.

problem:
Bookings, consultant schedules, and client appointments depended on manual records and Excel spreadsheets.

That created room for scheduling mistakes, conflicting appointments, and missed sessions when clients or consultants did not receive timely reminders.

The organization also needed to support online payments and virtual consultations without managing those interactions through separate disconnected tools.

The challenge was to turn the full consultation workflow into one digital operating platform.
solution:
Oraixen designed and developed Ghiras Al Usrah across web, mobile applications, backend services, APIs, and administration.

Clients can book supported consultation services, choose available appointments, request express consultations based on consultant availability, make payments through Moyasar, and attend supported virtual sessions through Zoom.

Consultants use a dedicated mobile application to manage schedules, set availability, review appointments, and access virtual consultations.

The administration platform centralizes the operational workflow that had previously depended on paper records and spreadsheets.
impact:
Booking, consultant availability, appointment management, reminders, payments, and supported virtual consultations can now be managed through a connected system instead of paper records and spreadsheets.

This gives clients, consultants, and administrators clearer visibility into appointments and reduces the operational risk created by manual scheduling and missing reminders.

title: Delora
description: A cosmetics e-commerce platform connecting product discovery, checkout, payments, and store operations across web and mobile.
cardDescription: A cosmetics commerce platform connecting product discovery, checkout, payments, and centralized store operations across web, iOS, and Android.
overview: Delora gives customers a dedicated beauty-shopping experience across web, iOS, and Android, while store teams manage products, orders, and customers through a centralized administration platform.

headings.challenge: A cosmetics brand needed more than a generic online store.
headings.build: A connected beauty-commerce platform across web, mobile, and administration.
headings.outcome: Delora launched a dedicated cosmetics commerce experience across web and mobile.

problem:
The client wanted to build a digital commerce experience specifically around makeup and cosmetics in Egypt.

The product needed to make beauty products easy to discover through clear categories, search, and filtering, while supporting a structured cart, checkout, and electronic payment journey.

The client also wanted to benchmark successful regional beauty-commerce experiences, including Nice One, while building a platform and brand experience tailored to Delora’s own market and customers.

Behind the customer experience, store teams needed one administration system for managing products, orders, and customer records.
solution:
Oraixen designed and developed Delora across the e-commerce website, iOS application, Android application, backend services, APIs, payment integrations, and administration.

Customers can browse a cosmetics-focused catalog, move through categories, search and filter products, add items to their cart, complete checkout, and use supported electronic payment methods.

Store managers use the administration platform to manage products, customer records, and orders from one central environment.

The customer experience was informed by benchmarking established regional commerce patterns while being designed around Delora’s own cosmetics offering.
impact:
Customers can discover beauty products, shop, complete checkout, and place orders through web, iOS, and Android experiences built around one commerce platform.

At the operational level, store teams can manage products, customers, and orders from one administration environment instead of operating each customer channel independently.

The result is a connected customer and store-management experience designed specifically around Delora’s cosmetics business.
